title: How to load multipart model multilingual-e5-large to Spring AI, how to combine .onnx and .onnx-data to single file/byte array?
body:
I apologize, being new to onnx...

I have already described the issue here, assuming that it si linkeed with onnxruntime:

https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/issues/21321

I would like to create "one consolidated onnx file" e.g. in some way to "merge" model.onnx and model onnx_data files

I understand that the principle of the issue is:
The current structure of initializer in model.onnx is always pointing to model_data (example):

```
  initializer {
    dims: 1024
    data_type: 1
    name: "encoder.layer.0.attention.output.LayerNorm.bias"
    external_data {
      key: "location"
      value: "model.onnx_data"
    }
    external_data {
      key: "offset"
      value: "1026146304"
    }
    external_data {
      key: "length"
      value: "4096"
    }
    data_location: EXTERNAL
  }
```

Expected resulting structure is without extarnal data, containing just raw_data (example):

```
  initializer {
    dims: 384
    data_type: 1
    name: "encoder.layer.0.attention.output.LayerNorm.bias"
    raw_data: "n\204v......."
```

I tried to:

load model.onnx
load model.onnx_data as ByteArray
change structure of the model

Final python code is:

```
def combine_onnx_files2(model_path, data_path, output_path):
    # Load the ONNX model structure
    model = onnx.load(model_path)

    # Load onnx_data
    with open(data_path, 'rb') as f:
        tensor_data = f.read()

    for initializer in model.graph.initializer:
        if initializer.data_location == onnx.TensorProto.EXTERNAL:
            offset = 0
            length = 0
            for data in initializer.external_data:
                if data.key == "offset":
                    offset = int(data.value)
                elif data.key == "length":
                    length = int(data.value)

            raw_data = tensor_data[offset:offset + length]

            del initializer.external_data[:]
            initializer.ClearField("data_location")

            initializer.raw_data = raw_data

    onnx.save(model, output_path)
```

Unfortunately:
protoc --decode=onnx.ModelProto onnx.proto < model_comb.onnx > output_comb.txt
is saying, that the structure is not correct...

What I am doing wrong?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
1. The combined file needs to be <2gb for it to be valid
2. Just do onnx.load and onnx.save without additional options will combine the file for you

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I have also tried to load/save the onnx file - resulting file has unfortunatly 2,08 Gb. When I try to validate - it is, as you say invalid.
My issue is how to utilize this model in Spring AI - see following issue, where I got one recommendation, which I am not able to implement...
[onnxruntime question](https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/issues/21321)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: I see. That may be a good question for the Spring AI developers

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: In the ORT issue you mentioned the api OrtSession(OrtEnvironment env, String modelPath, OrtAllocator allocator, SessionOptions options) right? Jus provide the path to the model file and the InferenceSession should be able to load the data file automatically for you

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Spring AI wants to load it from the classpath so it doesn't have a location on disk. Is there a spec for the `onnx_data` file format anywhere? I can add a method to ORT in Java that could read `onnx_data` files out into memory where they can be passed in as external initializers via the session options.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: onnx_data is just a plain file that stores the weights as bytes.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: But what's the format of the bytes? Do they have a shape array first then bytes or just bytes? Is there a marker between the tensors?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: It's just pure bytes. You can use the offset and length properties in the tensor proto message to obtain data for each tensor.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Ok, thanks. Are the floats stored little endian like protobuf, or is it platform dependent?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: I **think** they are little endian. May need to verify

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: Yes, they are little endian. The format is the same as that of `raw_data`, which is explained [here in the proto file](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/a850906190052fee780fe44a6c00c7ec4eac135b/onnx/onnx.in.proto#L605)

comments.author: reporter
participant2
comments.body: That might be a bug in the ORT create buffer logic. Try doing `byteBuffer.order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN).asFloatBuffer()` and then passing that to the `OnnxTensor.createTensor(OrtEnvironment, FloatBuffer, long[])` method. I'll try to run down the issue in the base method, we don't extensively test passing in byte buffers that are pretending to be other types and it looks like our validation is missing some cases.

comments.author: reporter
participant2
comments.body: There is a bug in the create buffer logic, I'll get it fixed next week.
